question.text: Using the precise (Fisher) effective real-rate formula, if the nominal rate of return on an investment is 7% and inflation is 6%, what is the real rate of return?

explanation.text: The Logic: The precise (Fisher) effective real-rate formula is Real rate = ((1 + nominal)/(1 + inflation)) - 1 = (1.07/1.06) - 1 = 0.009434, or approximately 0.94%. This is the answer required by p.20-21 of NISM Series XVII (Retirement Adviser, June 2025). The Trap: Options C (1.06%) and D (0.87%) are arithmetic distractors. Option A used to be 1.00%, which is the simple-subtraction approximation (7% - 6%) used in the workbook's narrative example on p.24. The original ambiguous stem did not specify which method to use, so both 0.94% (precise) and 1.00% (simple) were source-supported. Replacing the 1.00% distractor with 1.10% eliminates that ambiguity. Note: The original question was ambiguous because the source uses both the precise Fisher formula (p.20-21, giving 0.94%) and a simple subtraction approximation (p.24, giving 1.00%) with the same 7%/6% figures. The stem has been tightened to specify the precise/effective Fisher formula and the 1.00% distractor has been replaced so the keyed 0.94% answer is uniquely correct. Source: NISM Series XVII, June 2025, pp.20-21, 24.
